questions.explanation: Two hydroxido contribute -2 to the +3 metal, giving +1; aqua is neutral. Ignoring hydroxido charge would give +3.

questions.subject: CHEMISTRY
questions.topic: Alphabetical order of ligands in a name
questions.learningObjective: Explain alphabetical ordering of ligands in a name
questions.stem: An engineer's note asks why prefixes are ignored when alphabetising ligand names

answer.exemplar: Multiplicative prefixes such as di-, tri-, and tetra- indicate count, not identity, so ligands are alphabetised by their root names to keep the order independent of how many of each are present.

questions.explanation: Prefixes denote quantity, not identity, so they are ignored for ordering. Alphabetising by prefixed words would change order with count.

options.misconception: omits the prefix for a single ligand

questions.explanation: A single ligand uses the prefix mono-, often omitted in practice but conceptually mono-. Option D ignores the prefix concept.

questions.subject: CHEMISTRY
questions.learningObjective: Name an anionic complex correctly
questions.stem: A brief asks for the name of [AuCl4]-

answer.exemplar: The anionic complex is named tetrachloridoaurate(III) because four chlorido ligands are present, gold is +3, and the anionic charge requires the -ate suffix.

questions.explanation: Four chlorido ligands give tetrachlorido, gold is +3, and the anionic charge requires -ate. Omitting -ate would name a cation.

questions.topic: Formula that belongs to a stated name

questions.stem: A brief names sodium tetrachloridoaurate(III); how many sodium ions balance the complex?

questions.subject: CHEMISTRY
questions.learningObjective: Explain why coordination isomerism requires two complex ions
questions.stem: An engineer's note asks why a single complex ion cannot show coordination isomerism

answer.exemplar: Coordination isomerism requires two complex ions, one cationic and one anionic, so ligands can exchange between them; a single ion has no partner for exchange.

questions.explanation: A single ion cannot exchange ligands with itself in this sense. Confusing it with geometric isomerism misplaces the structural change.

questions.subject: CHEMISTRY
questions.learningObjective: Count coordinated water in a hydrate isomer
questions.stem: A brief gives the hydrate isomer [Cr(H2O)6]Cl3; how many water molecules are coordinated?
questions.explanation: All six water molecules are coordinated in [Cr(H2O)6]Cl3. Counting crystal water would add none here.
